Consumer sentiment falls in August after two previous months of improvement. The final August reading for the University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index came in at 51.7. This marks a 6.3% (3.5 points) decrease from July and below the preliminary reading of 51.0. Consumer sentiment sits 11.2% below where it was a year ago and is currently below the 1st percentile in the series' history.

results.content:
The University of Michigan updated its consumer sentiment index Friday with a preliminary August reading of 51, down about 8% from the final July index reading of 55.2.

The final August consumer sentiment index will be released on the 28th.

The school’s consumer sentiment tracker goes back decades and hit an all-time low in May. It had shown improvement across June and July before the downturn this month. results.title: Consumer sentiment falls in August as Americans 'just don't feel like they're thriving'

results.content: During his speech, the University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers released its final figures for August that showed consumer sentiment fell 6% compared with July and is now 11% lower than a year ago. Driven by worries that inflation will remain high into the future, the sentiment declines were across all political groups but fell most amongst among Republicans, older consumers, lower- and middle-income consumers and those without a college degree.
